To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liver growth is terminated by 2 months of age in mice.
the liver growth is a result of the increase in cell number and their weight, as well as the polyploidization.
the liver mass increases by 70% due to polyploidization and by 30% due to hypertrophy in the period from 0.5 to 1 month after birth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the postnatal mouse liver growth, which is based on the data on hepatocytes number and their weight as well as the ploidy distribution.
the quantitative analysis of the postnatal development of the liver in mice, which is a good model for studying the development of mammalian organs.

the analysis of the growth components of the liver, which is the largest organ in the organism, and is of great interest from the point of view of the development of the liver as a whole and its functional activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver mass is determined by the total number of cells and the protein content of a cell, and the latter two parameters change in a different way during ontogenesis.
the postnatal growth in the liver of the mouse is a result of the interaction of all three growth factors.
in the mouse liver the postnatal growth occurs via the following sequence of processes: polyploidization, hypertrophy, hyperplasia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the postnatal growth and development of the liver is a dynamic process of a complicated character.
the growth of the mouse hepatocytes is characterized by a high degree of polyploidization and a high rate of hyperplasia.
the liver mass in the mouse increases due to the increase in cell number and cell volume.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver mass is formed in a complex way.
the liver growth is not a single process, but rather a combination of different growth components.
the liver mass increases during the first month of life mainly due to the increase of the cell ploidy.
